v49_frozen_retrieval_benchmark.purpose: FAST MVP lane directive: the smallest executable retrieval/counter-authority benchmark that can falsify the product. The frozen reality benchmark measures recorded ANSWER artifacts; this one measures whether the frozen controlling authorities are reachable at all in independent OpenCaseLaw retrieval, in which query language, at what rank, with what duplicates and at what latency. Baseline = one plain /decisions search per (question, language, channel) with no query-map/counter-authority machinery, per the lane directive.

Authority sets re-owned from the frozen reality benchmark (sha ff57f556...); known-counter ids = union of counter-classified cited_decisions rows across accepted reality_check legs (label soundness NOT re-verified; stated in the spec).

falsifying_findings_38945976309.finding: A --offline re-run of the recorded retrieval benchmark turned the recorded FAIL of latency::full_pass_under_budget (256.827s vs the frozen 240s budget) into a PASS, because no gate read pass_a_mode and an offline pass overwrites pass_a_wall_seconds with the cache-read wall time (0.067s). The cycle report's own recommendation was to re-run from cache to confirm the verdict was stable; doing so deleted a preserved negative. overall_pass stayed false (12 failed/24 passed -> 11 failed/24 passed) so a summary reader would not have noticed.
falsifying_findings_38945976309.fix: evaluation/retrieval_gate/gates.py LIVE_PASS_MODE + _pass_a_not_live(); a latency gate may only pass/fail when pass A was live, otherwise not_measurable with an explicit reason. An undeclared pass_a_mode is treated conservatively as not measurable.
falsifying_findings_38945976309.not_weakened: no budget, threshold, token or gate success rule changed; --rescore of the recorded record still reproduces its stored verdict byte-for-byte after the change
falsifying_findings_38945976309.second_line_of_defence: The mode flag binds only what a record DECLARES. A record claiming pass_a_mode='live' with a hand-edited pass_a_wall_seconds would still be scored against the budget and could pass. gates.record_latency_plausibility() cross-checks a live record's wall time against its own timestamps (wall >= sum of its live per-search latencies; wall <= its started_at->generated_at span) so that forgery is caught. Deliberately NOT a gate: adding a gate would change the recorded verdict and destroy its byte-identity test.
